newsitem.title: INDIA: GAIL reports 12 percent rise in gas consumption.
newsitem.headline: GAIL reports 12 percent rise in gas consumption.

text.p: Gas consumption in India has risen 12 percent so far in 1997/98 (April-March) from last year's levels, C.R. Prasad, chairman and managing director of Gas Authority of India (GAIL) said on Monday.

"Last year it was an average of 48 million cubic metres per day supplied and this year we have already gone to 54 million cubic metres," the head of India's state-owned gas monopoly told an industry conference here.

"An expert committee of the planning commission... has projected almost a requirement of 200 million cubic metres of gas starting in the next five years," Prasad said at a symposium organised by the 'India Oil & Gas Review.'
GAIL is busy extending its pipeline network to reach major centres of demand.

"During last year we laid about 900 kilometres of pipeline," Prasad said adding that a major extension of India's largest pipeline network from the western state of Gujarat to North India, was underway, and consumer pipelines were also in progress.

In an interview with Reuters last month Prasad said GAIL's production was 64 million cubic metres a day and by 2002 it is expected to be 87 billion, indicating a supply shortfall despite recoverable reserves.

Offshore exploration in Burma and Bangladesh waters had yielded very good signs of discoveries, and a feasibility study had already been undertaken by Brown & Root, a subsidiary of Halliburton Co to bring gas ashore in India if the finds are confirmed.
Last week, the government announced merchant banks BZW, Morgan Stanley and Robert Fleming-Jardine Fleming will manage GAIL's planned issue of Global Depository Receipts (GDRs).
It said it planned to sell up to 25 percent of GAIL, which would reduce the government's stake in the gas monopoly to 71.63 percent.
The size of the GDR will depend on final pricing, but a merchant banker said he expected a $700-million GDR issue by GAIL.
